stages.line: In programming, these symbols are called operators. First, +: it combines values.
Next, -: it subtracts one value from another.
Now *: it multiplies values.
Last, /: it divides one value by another.
A program does two big things with values. First, it calculates, with arithmetic operators.

stages.line: 23 chocolates, 4 in each group. First, /: ordinary division, with decimals.
Next, //: floor division. It counts the complete groups.
Last, %: modulus. It gives what is left over.

stages.right: Floor division rounds the quotient down: the number of complete groups.
stages.wrong: // counts how many complete groups fit. It is not the leftover.
